text:
olivia: Heads-up — overnight we had a flurry of nodepool churn in eu-west-1 around 02:10 UTC. HPA spiked, CA added 6 gpu nodes, but ~10 pods stayed Pending for ~7m and then a bunch got evicted. Cost hit is noticeable. anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:

sam: can you paste the metric that fired the HPA? is it cpu/qps or a custom metric?

olivia: it's the external metric `service_latency_ms` (our realtime tail-latency aggregator). quick sample:
```
# PromQL (approx)
avg_over_time(service_latency_ms{job="frontend"}[1m]) > 250
# spike at 02:09..02:11: 260, 520, 380, 270 ms
```

mike: hmm sounds like cold-start spikes + probe jitter. HPA sees short burst -> creates pods -> CA spins nodes -> pods Pending because docker pulls + NV driver init + gpu plugin warming. by the time pods schedule the latency is back to normal so HPA scales down again. flapping.

rachel: are we running VPA recommender in the same namespace? VPA can restart pods to apply rightsizing which can add churn during a spike. also liveness/readiness probe backoff might be making the pod repeatedly fail initialisation.

olivia: we do have VPA in recommendation-only mode, but there are occasional restarts due to OOM until the recommendations land. readiness probe logs show `backoff 2s -> 8s` during that window.

autoscaler-bot: [02:12:07] cluster-autoscaler: ScaleUp triggered: nodepool-gpu-eu-west-1 +6 (requested by pod: frontend-realtime-####)
autoscaler-bot: [02:18:45] cluster-autoscaler: ScaleDown nodes: 4 (unneeded)

sam: two quick levers: 1) smooth the metric (longer window or an anomaly detector), 2) HPA.behavior with stabilizationWindowSeconds and select more conservative scaling rules. also consider external autoscaler gating (only scale if sustained > threshold for X minutes).

mike: another infra-level option: add a small warm pool of GPU nodes (1-2) in eu-west to handle short bursts instead of full CA ramp. Warm pool cheaper than on-demand churn if we keep for a few hours. also add node taint + pod toleration so only low-priority batch uses warm nodes.

rachel: for immediate mitigation we can increase `minReplicas` of HPA temporarily and extend `stabilizationWindowSeconds` to 300s. For longer-term: use smoothed quantile (p95 over 5m) instead of instantaneous avg.

olivia: cost note: overnight CA churn added ~0.6 GPU-days this week in eu-west; rough extra = ~$420. not huge but recurring.

sam: we should also tune kubelet imagePullPolicy / use pre-baked AMI with nvidia drivers + containerd caches to cut boot time from ~90s to ~15s. that reduces the scheduling delay a lot.

mike: here's a suggested HPA snippet to try (small change):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: frontend-realtime
spec:
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 40
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: service_latency_ms
      target:
        type: Value
        value: "250"
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 180
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 50
        periodSeconds: 60
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
```

rachel: also create a CA annotation to bump `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to something like 10m for that nodepool, and `--max-node-provision-time` for our cloud provider if supported.

olivia: ok action items: 1) sam to open PR to switch HPA metric to p95 5m + apply behavior window (short-term) 2) mike to prototype warm-pool (infra) 3) rachel to adjust CA flags & check VPA restart frequency. I'll add cost estimate to the ticket.

sam: will do PR, include comparative graphs (instant vs p95) and link to the spike logs.

mike: I'll spin up a 1-node warm-pool in staging and run a synthetic spike to measure cold-start delta.

rachel: I'll audit VPA events for the namespace and see if any recent recommendation updates caused restarts around 02:00.

olivia: thanks all. tagging @oncall-sre for visibility. I'll update thread after PR merges. :thumbsup:
